title: Solution Architecture & Software for the Next-Generation Vehicle Inspection System
capability_statement:
Parsons proposes a complete, end-to-end Inspection Program software platform built around a centralized Inspection Database (the NGVID-equivalent of our existing VIID), a configurable rules engine for inspection logic, a managed workstation software stack at testing facilities, secure web-services integration with the State Motor Vehicle agency, and a multi-AZ AWS-hosted infrastructure that has carried sister programs at 99.99-100% uptime. The capability covers six clusters of obligations the RFP groups under Solution Architecture & Software:

(1) Centralized Inspection Database and core data model. The Inspection Database is the single repository for all program data: specified vehicle data drawn from State motor-vehicle files, prior inspection results, sticker and station/inspector/repair-technician records, manufacturer recall and Technical Service Bulletin data, Master Reference Tables, calibration and oversight data, lift/suspension/waiver/repair/remote-sensing data, and the version numbers of all deployed workstation software and firmware [chunks 2074, 2075, 2093]. Every record uploaded from test analyzers is stored in raw form first and then processed for accuracy and validation, with redundancy and backup strategies engineered for zero data loss [chunks 2078, 2079]. Three distinct VIN checks (decode, validate, prior-inspection lookup) minimize unmatched transactions and cross-reference model year, make, model, engine, emissions control systems, cut points, prior pass/fail and recall status before a test begins [chunk 2078]. The database keeps test data online for the entirety of the contract and remains retrievable for 180 days after expiration, with covert audit records held to the same retention rule [chunk 2067].

(2) Workstation software stack and inspection-floor experience. Parsons supplies the workstation application that drives every inspection at testing facilities, with common user interfaces, communications routines, data processing and quality assurance across all developed applications [chunk 2091]. The workstation pre-populates vehicle data on the operator screen for validation rather than re-keying, surfaces history alerts and special-handling notes for the vehicle under test, presents prior inspection results so the correct initial-or-reinspection procedure runs, and enforces equipment parameters set by the manufacturer [chunks 2079, 2080]. When the workstation cannot reach the central database, equipment continues operating offline so the public is not turned away, and transactions reconcile when connectivity returns [chunk 2050]. The same stack supports legacy TSI dial-up analyzers and modern OBD/VIS Internet-based analyzers in a single database, including equipment as much as 26 years old, which is a documented program-risk reducer for jurisdictions transitioning from legacy fleets [chunks 2053, 2074].

(3) Rules-driven test logic and fraud-prevention analytics. The platform's processing layer applies inspection rules at first call and end of test (vehicle look-up, VIN decode, prior-result reconciliation, blind emissions test handling) and feeds an analytics layer of audit triggers that flag data anomalies indicating potential fraudulent testing or repair [chunks 2078, 2079]. Fraud-prevention triggers are continuously tuned by drawing on data from sister Inspection Programs [chunk 2079]. Cross-program inputs and analytic audit triggers are positioned in the proposal as an active fraud-detection capability rather than only a reporting function.

(4) Workstation-to-database integration and authentication. Inspection Test Units reach the central database through secure web services; State personnel reach portals, reporting and ad-hoc query through secure protocols on the public internet; and the Parsons operations team manages the system through encrypted channels [chunks 2062, 2064]. A two-call security model is used: at the start of every communication the database verifies the request originates from a valid station, and a station-generated token encoding date/time, the analyzer's PAS ID and the station ID is decoded server-side; for legacy dial-up TSI units, Automatic Number Identification (ANI) on the inbound phone line is also validated; a static IP address may be used as an additional check where the station's ISP does not change [chunks 2075, 2076, 2081]. Only assigned analyzers and inspectors with the correct credentials may submit, and unverifiable connections are blocked [chunk 2081].

(5) Cloud-hosted, high-availability architecture. The proposed architecture runs in AWS across two active availability zones behind Route 53 DNS, AWS WAF and Shield, CloudFront with TLS termination, and an application load balancer; application microservices run on AWS Fargate with auto-recovery and auto-scaling; the relational store is multi-AZ Aurora MySQL with six-way volume replication and automatic failover, fronted by S3 for static content, archiving and logs, with a serverless compute tier and QuickSight for BI [chunks 2062, 2063, 2065]. Backups are daily, real-time, full and incremental using snapshots, with cross-AZ and cross-region replication via AWS Backup, and version-controlled application code in the daily backup window [chunks 2031, 2032]. Most maintenance and upgrades are performed without downtime because critical components are AWS managed services [chunks 2088, 2090]. Source code is escrowed with Iron Mountain under Parsons' Master Escrow Agreement, with the State named as beneficiary [chunks 2058, 2059].

(6) Reporting, ad-hoc query and outbound data exchange. A web-based reporting suite with role-based security supports formatting, filtering, sorting, grouping, aggregations, summary calculations, crosstab/grid/chart presentation, dashboards, drill-down, scheduling, web/email sharing, and PDF/CSV/Excel export [chunks 2068, 2069]. Ad-hoc tools and training are delivered to State staff so they can build their own operational reports without IT support, and Parsons supplies written analyses for queries on request [chunk 2069]. Daily inspection-data transmission to the State runs today over secure Electronic File Transfer with a documented willingness to switch to a real-time web-services interface in parallel with State system changes; either batch or web-service API can push data into the State data warehouse [chunks 2059, 2061, 2064]. The same channel carries lockouts, emission-control system data, Technical Service Bulletins, recalls and electronic technical bulletins to comply with EPA Rules at 40 CFR section 51.369 [chunk 2061].

differentiators: Parsons is the only vendor with a working multi-protocol inspection platform that concurrently supports three legacy dial-up TSI analyzers and three IP-based OBD/VIS analyzers in one central database, with the network hardware already operationally positioned to keep legacy fleets in service - which directly de-risks the State's transition from a Legacy VID to an NGVID architecture [chunks 2053, 2056, 2074]. The proposed AWS landing zone has been independently audited and carries SOC 1, 2 and 3, PCI, and ISO 9001/27001/27017/27018 attestations [chunk 2058], and the same team that completed the Ontario DriveON heavy-duty emissions migration to AWS with no station-side impact would execute this migration [chunks 2057, 2058, 2084]. DevSecOps is built into the SDLC with code-scan and vulnerability-scan gates configured to State and industry thresholds, centralized via AWS Security Hub, and the cybersecurity practice scans Inspection Database systems with the same technology used for high-sensitivity US government programs [chunks 1973, 2084]. Operational resilience is reinforced by daily real-time full and incremental backups using specialized archiving software and snapshots, cross-AZ and cross-region replication via AWS Backup, version-controlled code in the same backup window, and an Iron Mountain source-code escrow with the State named as beneficiary [chunks 2031, 2032, 2058, 2059]. A reporting suite with built-in dashboards, drill-down, scheduling and PDF/CSV/Excel export plus ad-hoc tools placed in the hands of State staff is already in production on multiple programs [chunks 2068, 2069]. Finally, the proposal commits that the State owns all data and that contract-end, early-termination and termination-for-cause data hand-back terms will be honored [chunk 2058].
gap_notes:
The evidence corpus for this theme is heavy on architecture, hosting, backups, integration patterns, reporting, fraud analytics and past performance - but several high-priority RFP obligations under Solution Architecture & Software are NOT directly substantiated in the supplied chunks and need targeted proposal text or commitment language sourced elsewhere:
- A-008 (sec 1.2.5) and R-036 (sec 4.1.1): explicit commitment to deliver an NGVID that replaces a Legacy VID is implied by Parsons' VIID experience but the chunks do not contain a direct 'we will deliver NGVID' statement aligned to State labels.
- A-073 (sec 4.1.1): pre-rollout legacy-data population of NGVID is not described in evidence; evidence references successful AWS migrations but not a populate-from-legacy step.
- A-071 (sec 4.1) and A-077 (sec 4.2): 18-month transition window and complete delivery at end of Implementation Phase are not directly committed in the chunks.
- A-079 (sec 4.23.2.6.A) and A-034 (sec 4.34.2): the RFP requires Oracle RDBMS aligned to the State Motor Vehicle agency's version, while the proposed architecture is Aurora MySQL (chunks 2063, 2065). This is a substantive architecture conflict that must be resolved (dual-engine, Oracle target, or formal deviation).
- A-022 (sec 4.23.2.10): commitment to multiple standalone DEV/UAT/PROD environments is not present in the chunks.
- A-040 (sec 4.23.A) and A-033 (sec 4.22.B): obligation to supply or develop and test all NGVID components and ancillary support is not enumerated.
- M-013 (sec 4.22.B.7) and M-006 (sec 4.22.A.5): real-time hot backups of production databases is partially supported by the daily-real-time backup language (chunks 2031, 2032) but the term 'hot backup' and the specific NGVID database list are not present.
- R-020 (sec 4.26.4): XML formatting for all NGWorkstation-NGVID transactions is not mentioned in evidence.
- R-058 (sec 4.27.2): the five external-facing web interfaces are not enumerated.
- A-009 (Appendix 3.5B): use of WS-Security to validate clients and encrypt SOAP messages is not in the chunks.
- R-066 (sec 3.2J Part 1 OBD), A-004 (sec 4.19.3.A), A-014 (sec 4.20.1.A), A-022 (sec 4.20.2), A-027 (sec 4.20.3), A-075 (sec 4.20.7.3.A.7), A-082 (sec 4.20.7.5), R-045 (sec 3.2H): NGWorkstation hardware composition (OBD interface, integrated smoke meters, NJDEP-certified diesel opacity, drive-on/stop brake testers) is not in the supplied chunks - the workstation evidence is software-side only.
- R-049 (sec 4.19.1) and A-084 (sec 4.20.8.1.A): explicit commitment that NGWorkstations are operational and communicating with NGVID before/during/after each inspection is not directly stated.
- A-086 (sec 4.20.8.1.B): HTTPS plus State-authorized login credentials at the workstation is not enumerated (TLS at the edge is present in chunks 2062, 2064 but not at the workstation login layer).
- R-014 (sec 4.20.8.3.C) and R-015 (sec 4.20.8.3.C): NGWorkstation -> NGVID inspection-history call and NGVID -> State Motor Vehicle agency data feed are conceptually supported by the architecture but not explicitly described.
- R-026 (sec 4.20.8.3.F): VIN decoder in all workstations is implied by the three-VIN-checks language (chunk 2078) but the chunk places decoding server-side, not workstation-side.
- R-072 (sec 4.20.8.3.M): blind emissions test is not stated in evidence.
- R-113 (sec 4.20.9.1.A), R-120 (sec 4.20.9.2.A), R-055 (sec 3.2J Fail Actions), M-012 (Appendix 3.4B): workstation lockouts, barcode/PIN authentication and unauthorized-access protection at the workstation are not described - server-side token/ANI controls are present (chunks 2075, 2076, 2081) but not the workstation-side controls.
- A-099 (sec 4.2): collection and storage of inspection plus MIT and BIT data is not mentioned.
- A-080 (sec 4.24.3.B.12): 30-minute notification on loss of major functionality is not stated; chunk 2090 commits to monthly downtime reports and incident-time reporting in general terms.
- A-056/A-057/A-058 (sec 3.4A-12.4-6): communications-rate SLAs of 99.9%/99.0%/95% by category are not directly committed; uptime metrics in chunks 2028 and 2090 are availability not communications-rate metrics.
- A-026 (sec 3.4A-3): final OBD test design subject to State approval is not stated.
- R-098 (sec 4.28.3.3.C.9): stress/load test profile of 20,000/50,000 transactions per 8-hour day is not in evidence.
- R-002, R-004, R-007, R-026, R-033, R-059, R-064, R-065, R-100, R-104, R-105, R-110, R-113, R-115 (sec 4.28.x): the full ATP program (independent ATPs for new NGWorkstations, written SCM approval before testing, beta testing of the entire NGSystem, end-to-end ATP, EPA/SAE J1667/State OBD compliance demonstration, accuracy verification, OBD coverage across vehicle types, beta-summary, Architecture and Design Specification compliance, quantitative performance per Requirements Specification, Security and BC/DR Plan SCM approval, custom source code deposit in a git repository with the State) is not directly substantiated in the chunks; ATP capability is referenced at a high level only (chunks 2090, 2091, 2093).
- R-014/A-058/A-059 (rules engine - Begin/EndTest cycles, terminate ruleset on invalid attributes, run reset rulesheets even on terminated ruleset, terminate inspection on invalid mvcRegCode): the supplied evidence describes inspection logic and analytics in general but does not surface the specific rulesheet/ruleset semantics the RFP appendices require.
- A-015 (sec 4.30.2): data integrity, security and content during migration is committed in spirit by Parsons' AWS migration record (chunks 2057, 2084) but not specifically tied to the NGVID migration.
- A-025 (sec 4.31): NGSystem maintenance, repair or replacement obligation is not stated as an explicit lifecycle commitment.
- A-012 (sec 4.7.A): Issue Tracking System is referenced indirectly in chunk 2090 ('issues are logged and categorized in our issue tracking software') but not as a documented ITS deliverable.
- A-010 (sec 4.24.1): the contract-term 'no major security breach' obligation is supported by Parsons' breach-free track record (chunk 2084) but is not a contractual commitment statement.
- Compliance-and-personnel obligations grouped under this theme by the data pipeline (A-003 no auto-renewal, M-007 fair/open process, R-080 bidder responsibility, A-022 background checks, R-027/A-028 organizational experience, R-028 location info, R-029/A-030 org chart, R-030/A-031 resumes, R-031/A-040 contracts of similar size and scope, R-032/A-047 financial capability, R-014 non-discrimination, A-040 security engineering, A-045 protective tech for configuration verification, A-038 cloud design per agreed service/security levels, R-022/R-031 SDLC, R-050 third-party risk) are scoped by other catalog themes; for this theme the gap is that the evidence carries only adjacent material (cybersecurity practice in chunks 1973, 1974, 1983, 2042, 2084 and SDLC/DevSecOps in chunk 2084) and a fully sourced response will need pull-throughs from the corporate, security and program-management themes.
- Pricing-tied obligations (R-033 price sheet, A-052 firm pricing) are not addressable from architecture evidence and belong to the pricing theme.
